guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, one_hot_err_q, kmac_done_err_q, and cmd_consty_err_q are cleared to 0.
When rst_ni is high, on every positive edge of clk_i, one_hot_err_q follows one_hot_err_d, kmac_done_err_q follows kmac_done_err_d, and cmd_consty_err_q follows cmd_consty_err_d.

assumptions.claim: The asynchronous reset input rst_ni must meet standard recovery/removal timing with respect to the clk_i positive edge to avoid metastable error register values.
assumptions.risk: Metastable one_hot_err_q, kmac_done_err_q, or cmd_consty_err_q could propagate incorrect error status to key manager control logic, potentially causing false error handling or missing real faults.

uncertain_points.claim: The error registers update every cycle without latching; if the _d inputs are combinational error conditions that de-assert after the condition clears, the _q outputs also de-assert immediately. The design intent on error persistence (sticky until cleared) is unclear, risking transient errors being missed by software or error handling logic.
uncertain_points.cond: When an error event is transient.
uncertain_points.risk: Transient integrity errors (one-hot, kmac done, command constancy) may be lost, leading to undetected faults during key management operations.

uncertain_points.claim: Errors asserted while rst_ni is low will not be captured because the registers are held in reset; after reset deassertion, only error conditions present at or after the first post-reset clock edge are registered. This creates a window where a persistent error active during reset could be missed.
uncertain_points.cond: When an error condition exists during reset.
uncertain_points.risk: A latent fault present at startup (e.g., a stuck-at error) may be missed, allowing key management operations to proceed in a faulty state.
